feature: izba desktop app — Display tab (VNC desktop)

journeys.rationale: The Display tab's cheapest, most common path: a sandbox created without a desktop shows the not-enabled explainer and an Enable affordance, and flipping it on for an ALREADY-RUNNING sandbox must be honest that the change is not live yet — the guest needs the kasmvnc.erofs disk + izba.vnc=1 cmdline that only a fresh boot attaches, so the tab must show the restart banner (not silently pretend the desktop is reachable, and not embed a stale iframe).

source.ref: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-vnc-display-design.md §9 PR2 sketch (GUI); DisplayTab.tsx not-enabled/restart-required rendering; vnc.ts vncPresentation restart-required precedence

steps.intent: type {workspace} into the Workspace field, 'vnc-enable-demo' into the Name field, and 'alpine:3.20' into the Image field, leaving the 'Desktop (VNC)' checkbox unchecked, then click Create to create a new sandbox from this workspace
steps.expect: a sandbox named vnc-enable-demo appears in the sandbox list

steps.intent: open the vnc-enable-demo sandbox's detail view and click its Display tab
steps.expect: the Display tab shows 'Run a full Linux desktop in this sandbox, streamed to your browser.' and an 'Enable desktop' button, with no desktop iframe and no restart banner

steps.intent: on the sandbox's Overview, click Start to boot it; wait until its status shows running
click the Display tab and click 'Enable desktop'
steps.expect: the Display tab shows 'Restart the sandbox to apply the desktop change.' alongside a Restart button, and still no desktop iframe appears — the desktop is enabled in config but not yet live on the running guest
steps.expect_text: Restart the sandbox to apply the desktop change.

journeys.rationale: The flagship promise: a sandbox created and started WITH the desktop already enabled must, once the guest is up, show a live embedded desktop and an Open-in-browser escape hatch — and it must do so without ever putting the desktop's credential (carried in `vnc_url`'s userinfo, per DisplayTab.tsx's CREDENTIAL DISCIPLINE comment) anywhere a screen or the DOM could leak it: the iframe embeds the credential-less loopback proxy (`api.vncProxyStart`), never the raw `vnc_url`, and neither Open in browser nor Copy URL render the URL as text. This journey does NOT assert anything about the desktop's rendered pixels (KasmVNC content) — only the UI's own truthful state: the iframe exists, the controls exist, and no plaintext secret is visible.

source.ref: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-vnc-display-design.md §6 Credentials + §9 PR2 sketch (GUI); DisplayTab.tsx CREDENTIAL DISCIPLINE comment + iframe embed (title="Sandbox desktop"); vnc.ts CREDENTIAL DISCIPLINE comment

steps.intent: type {workspace} into the Workspace field, 'vnc-live-demo' into the Name field, and 'alpine:3.20' into the Image field, check the 'Desktop (VNC)' checkbox, then click Create to create a new sandbox from this workspace with the desktop enabled
steps.expect: a sandbox named vnc-live-demo appears in the sandbox list

steps.intent: open the vnc-live-demo sandbox's detail view and, on its Overview, click Start to boot the sandbox; wait until its status shows running
click the Display tab and wait for the desktop to come up
steps.expect: the Display tab shows an embedded desktop iframe (titled 'Sandbox desktop'), an 'Open in browser' button, and a 'Copy URL' button — and no plaintext password or credential string appears anywhere on the page, in the visible text, the iframe's src, or any other attribute
